rationale: These are the thresholds `bun run eval:live-parity` fails on, and they are data rather than constants for the reason R6a's calibration margins are data: a number that lives inside the file that reads it gets widened by whoever is trying to make the run green. Each one is set from the size of the failure it must catch, not from the size of the noise it must tolerate. maxCosineDistance 0.002: an embedding endpoint is deterministic for a fixed model id and input, so the honest expected divergence is zero and this window covers float32 round-tripping through base64 and JSON only; the failures it must catch are far larger — a swapped asymmetric encoding moves a U7 fixture vector by roughly 0.04 (ENCODING_WEIGHT is 0.15 of a unit rotation) and a changed prefix by more, so there are more than ten binary orders of magnitude of headroom between real noise and real breakage. `evals/live-parity.ts` refuses any value above 0.02 for exactly that reason. maxComponentDelta 0.002 exists because cosine is scale- and shape-forgiving in a way a per-component check is not: a handful of components moving a long way can leave the angle almost unchanged, and that is what a partially-changed input template looks like. unitNormEpsilon 0.001 is tight on purpose — KTD8 pins truncation to the API's `dimensions` parameter precisely because the parameter re-normalises and a client-side slice does not, so a vector arriving at 0.87 length is the signature of that bug and nothing else; float32 accumulation over 1536 components does not move a unit norm by anything close to 1e-3. maxScoreDelta 0.01 is the loosest of the four and is provisional: cross-encoder scores are not committed yet (U12), so this number has never been measured against a real distribution and the first live rerank run is what should replace it. Revisit all four when the first provider-sourced manifest lands; a tolerance that has never once been exercised is an estimate, and this file should say so rather than imply otherwise.
